final_message:
I reproduced the bug at 4f08332 (bundled `@eslint/config-array` 0.18.0). The `F:\foo.js` file gets linted instead of being ignored, and this happens in both `Linter#verify` and `ESLint`. This VM runs Linux, so I didn't run it on real Windows. Instead, the script makes every `require("path")` return `path.win32` and sets the working directory to `C:\Project`.

Run from the repo root: `node repro/windows-cross-drive.js` (it exits with 1 when the bug shows up).

| File | `path.win32.relative(cwd, file)` | Linter / ESLint result |
|---|---|---|
| `C:\Project\foo.js` | `"foo.js"` | linted (correct) |
| `C:\other\foo.js` | `"..\\other\\foo.js"` | ignored: "No matching configuration found" / "File ignored because outside of base path" (correct) |
| `F:\foo.js` | `"F:\\foo.js"` | **linted: `no-undef: 'foo' is not defined.`**, and `isPathIgnored` returns `false` (bug) |

**Likely cause:** in `node_modules/@eslint/config-array/dist/cjs/index.cjs`, `getConfigWithStatus()` (around line 953) and `shouldIgnorePath()` (around line 502) decide a file is outside the base path only when `path.relative(basePath, filePath)` starts with `".."`. When the two paths are on different drives, Windows returns the target path unchanged (`F:\foo.js`). That doesn't start with `".."`, so the file counts as inside the base path, matches the universal config and gets linted. A check that also rejects an absolute result (`path.isAbsolute(rel)`) would cover this case.

**Limits:**
- The simulation only covers pure path logic. I didn't test `lintFiles`, which is what the CLI uses with a real `F:\` file, because that reads the real filesystem. It goes through the same config-array check.
- If you want confirmation on real Windows, I can run it on a Windows machine.

The patch adds only repro/windows-cross-drive.js.
